tomato early blight.symptoms: Dark brown round spots with rings inside them (a target or bullseye look), usually on the older, lower leaves first. A yellow halo often forms around each spot, and badly affected leaves turn yellow and dry up. Dark sunken spots can also appear on stems and near the fruit stalk.
look_alikes: Septoria leaf spot (many small spots with grey centres)
Late blight (large, water-soaked patches, white growth in wet weather)
tomato early blight.favourable_weather: Warm weather with high humidity, dew or frequent rain. Plants that are stressed, heavily loaded with fruit or short of nutrients are hit harder.

weather_profile.note: No verified numbers loaded yet. Add them from TNAU or MPKV.

organic_control: Pick off and destroy the badly affected lower leaves, and do not leave them lying in the field
Water at the base of the plant and avoid wetting the leaves
Mulch the soil so rain does not splash spores onto the leaves
Stake or tie plants so leaves stay off the soil
tomato early blight.chemical_control: Use only a product that is registered in India for this crop and disease. Check the label or ask your agriculture officer for the product, dose and spray interval. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Rotate with crops outside the tomato, potato, brinjal and chilli family
Keep plants spaced so air moves between them
Clear old tomato and potato residue after harvest
Feed the crop properly, because weak plants get the disease worse
tomato early blight.when_to_call_expert: If spots are spreading to the upper leaves or fruit within days, or if many plants are affected.

UC IPM, tomato pest management guidelines

tomato late blight.cause: Water mold (Phytophthora infestans), a fungus-like organism that also attacks potato
tomato late blight.symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked patches on leaves that turn olive and then brown or black. In wet weather a white to grey fuzzy growth appears at the edge of the patches, mostly on the underside of the leaf. Stems and leaf stalks darken, and fruit gets large firm brown spots. In cool wet weather whole plants can collapse within about a week to ten days.
look_alikes: Early blight (spots with clear rings, usually smaller)
tomato late blight.favourable_weather: Cool to moderate temperatures with very high humidity, fog, heavy dew or rain, and leaves that stay wet for many hours. Hot, dry weather slows it down.

weather_profile.note: Moderate temperatures (about 15 to 27 C) with humidity near 90 percent or more and long leaf wetness, from university extension sources.

organic_control: Remove and destroy infected plants or plant parts quickly, away from the field, because infected plants cannot be saved
Avoid overhead watering and irrigating late in the day
Remove volunteer tomato and potato plants and nearby solanaceous weeds
tomato late blight.chemical_control: Use only a product that is registered in India for this crop and disease. Protective sprays matter most in cool, wet spells, so ask your agriculture officer for the product, dose and spray interval. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Use healthy seedlings and avoid seedlings from fields with the disease
Plant with wide spacing and stake plants for airflow
Scout often in cool, wet or foggy weather, because the disease moves fast
Do not plant tomato next to a potato field with blight
Choose varieties with some tolerance if your KVK recommends them
tomato late blight.when_to_call_expert: At the first large water-soaked patches, especially in cool wet weather, because it spreads in days.
